targets.claim: Ambush attacks on police officers have been the leading cause of felonious deaths of law enforcement officers for the past five years.
Google continues to promote a smartphone app called Waze that allows criminals to track the location of police officers.
Waze is a popular real-time traffic app that uses GPS navigation and crowdsourcing to alert users about traffic jams, accidents, and the presence of law enforcement.
Most users likely use the app to avoid traffic tickets, but it poses a significant risk to police officers.
The man who killed two New York police officers used Waze to monitor the movements of police officers.
Google claims the app contributes to the 'common good' on the road.
The risks far outweigh any potential benefits.
It only takes a few clicks for users to identify the location of police officers, making them vulnerable targets.
The app can also be used by perpetrators of domestic violence, gang members, narcotics dealers, and potential terrorists.
Despite Google's reputation for corporate social responsibility, the company has refused to discuss the issue with organizations representing law enforcement.
The National Sheriffs' Association has called on Google to prioritize the safety of both motorists and police officers.
